A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOVELQR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original recommendation experiments, LLM diagnostic evaluations, user studies, ablations and human annotation analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and the four user studies in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The label agent, retrieval followed by label filtering, and novelty/popularity/match reranking procedure remain unchanged. Section 4 and the appendices retain the same token-weighting formulas and correction steps.

E1.justification: QuoteR, QUILL and the authors' three-domain benchmark retain the same coverage and 100 instances each. NOVELQR-BENCH is a rename of NOVELQR, not an added dataset. Diagnostic evaluations and user-study scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same generation, retrieval, reranking and novelty-estimation baselines. This includes QuoteR, QUILL, bm25, Bge-large, Qwen3-Re, GPT and Self-BLEU. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 revises popularity-count collection from 'averaged UTC snapshots' to 'fixed UTC snapshots,' retaining the February–April 2025 window. This is a limited revision to the reported preprocessing protocol; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Other stated evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same retrieval, label-filter, model-size, novelty-weighting, popularity and judge-robustness analyses are retained. V2's four-case Figure 6 relocates v1's Appendix N Figure 16; it does not introduce additional cases.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly states that Match and Novelty scores are averaged over three random seeds. V1 already documented three judge repetitions in Appendix G. The revision adds explicit seed/averaging information without establishing increased runs; bootstrap procedures and confidence intervals remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Qwen3-32B's Match score from 3.45 to 4.45 under otherwise unchanged reported conditions. Its Novelty score of 3.77 and ranking metrics remain unchanged. Other matched table values and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: The novelty-score definitions and derivations in Section 4.3 and Appendix L, and comparator definitions in Appendix M, remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its empirical wording: explicit superiority in appropriateness, novelty and engagement becomes human preference and overall recommendation quality, while 'matching or surpassing' novelty estimators becomes 'competitive' estimation. The three methodological contributions and conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5.5 adds an explicit scalability argument that enlarging the quotation pool increases offline preprocessing approximately linearly while online serving remains practical. Appendix I already discussed caching and latency, but this pool-growth interpretation is newly stated. Subjectivity limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code hyperlink in the abstract and states that popularity counts are reported in the knowledge base for reproducibility. Existing hardware, caching, latency and prompt details are retained. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's availability or contents.

R1.justification: V2 adds quotation-recommendation references by Ahn et al. (2016), Tan et al. (2016, 2018) and Wang et al. (2021, 2022) to the introduction and related work. This broadens citation coverage while retaining the existing relevance-versus-novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V2 shortens and rewrites the abstract, removes duplicated discussion in Section 5.2, adds an experimental roadmap and cost subsection, and promotes the case study to a standalone section. Benchmark terminology and acknowledgements also change; most body and appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: Much of the appendix changes from full-width text to two-column layout, substantially reflowing annotation instructions, mathematical explanations, prompts and the questionnaire. The four-case appendix figure becomes main-text Figure 6, replacing the single-case display and eliminating duplication. These are extensive layout changes despite stable scientific content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reporting and readability through clearer abstract claims, removal of repeated prose, explicit seed averaging and a code pointer. The revised Table 2 value also removes the apparent large-model Match drop that conflicted with the accompanying robustness interpretation. These are limited gains: the added scalability argument has no new measurements, and Appendix I's runtime evidence remains unchanged.
